d: Primary exports (must each get a real U()/UN() call): timeGetTime, timeGetSystemTime, timeGetDevCaps, timeBeginPeriod, timeEndPeriod. Timer basics, all five are winmm 7-byte jmp thunks into kernel32 (api-ms-win-mm-time-l1-1-0): timeGetTime (ord 141), timeGetSystemTime (140), timeGetDevCaps (139), timeBeginPeriod (137), timeEndPeriod (138). Verified gates [decomp kernel32 0x22840/0x1e110/0x1d190/0x6a040 + VM fc02probe]: timeGetDevCaps(NULL, sizeof) and (p, 7) -> 97 TIMERR_NOCANDO (not TIMERR_STRUCT, not INVALPARAM); (p, 8) -> 0 with wPeriodMin >= 1 (1 on the VM) and wPeriodMax == 1000000; a larger cb (e.g. 16) also 0 and bytes past 8 untouched (verify in decomp, else t_note). timeGetSystemTime(NULL,12) and (p,11) -> 129 TIMERR_STRUCT; (p,12) -> 0, wType == TIME_MS(1), u.ms within a few ms of timeGetTime(); a 16-byte MMTIME with wType preset to TIME_SAMPLES comes back TIME_MS. timeGetTime monotonic over a bounded loop (no decrease across 1000 calls, advances across Sleep(50) by >= 30 and < 2000), in step with GetTickCount (|diff| small, t_note the delta, no hard bound below ~100 ms). timeBeginPeriod/EndPeriod counting contract: Begin(0) -> 97, End(0) -> 97; Begin(1)/End(1) -> 0/0 then End(1) -> 97; nested Begin(2) x2 needs two Ends, third -> 97; unbalanced End(7) -> 97; period 15 is counted (End twice -> second 97); periods >= uMax (16 on the VM: derive uMax = ceil(NtQueryTimerResolution max/10000) at run time, never hard-code 16) such as 16, 1000, 0xFFFFFFFF are uncounted no-ops (Begin 0, End 0, End again 0). Every Begin is paired before the test returns (SAFETY). Observable effect: after Begin(1) NtQueryTimerResolution current <= 10000 (t_note; global resolution is max over processes, so only CHECK that it is not coarser than before). Also: address identity -- decode the winmm thunk (FF 25 rel32) and CHECK the IAT target equals GetProcAddress(kernel32, same name) (UIN("kernel32.dll", timeGetTime)). Threads: timeGetTime from 4 threads concurrently stays monotonic per thread. Headless, no device. Consumers: Chrome, mstscax, quartz, industrial cycle timing.

Primary exports (must each get a real U()/UN() call): timeSetEvent, timeKillEvent. timeSetEvent (ord 143) / timeKillEvent (ord 142), local winmm bodies (0x2a20/0x2e50, worker timeThread). Verified [decomp + VM pass 2]: fuEvent & 0xFFFFFE0E -> returns 0 (e.g. 2, 0x200, 0x8000); valid bits TIME_ONESHOT 0, TIME_PERIODIC 1, TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_SET 0x10, TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_PULSE 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS 0x100. uDelay 0 -> 0, uDelay 1000001 -> 0, uDelay 1000000 accepted (kill immediately); uDelay < wPeriodMin -> 0. uResolution 0 and huge values are clamped, not rejected. Return ids are nonzero, id = generation(step 0x10) + slot(id & 0xF), not reused for the next allocation. One-shot TIME_CALLBACK_FUNCTION fires exactly once with (uTimerID == returned id, uMsg == 0, dwUser == passed value, dw1 == 0, dw2 == 0) on a thread that is not the caller (GetCurrentThreadId differs; t_note the priority, TIME_CRITICAL expected, verify in decomp); killing an already-fired one-shot -> 97; killing a live periodic -> 0 and a second kill -> 97; timeKillEvent(0x12345) -> 97. NEVER use id 0 as 'unknown' (timeKillEvent(0) matches a free slot once the timer thread exists and returns 0 [VM]); a dedicated test may CHECK timeKillEvent(0) -> 97 only in a CHILD process that has never called timeSetEvent. TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_SET: fptc is an auto/manual event HANDLE, WaitForSingleObject(ev, 2000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0; periodic EVENT_SET signals repeatedly (count >= 3 in 500 ms at 50 ms period, loose bound). TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_PULSE on a manual-reset event: a waiter blocked before the tick wakes, the event is not left signalled afterwards. NULL function callback one-shot: returns a nonzero id, later kill -> 97 [VM]. Periodic count over 1 s at 20 ms between 25 and 75 (loose) and periodic re-arm from scheduled time (t_note drift). dwUser passes full 64-bit value. Bounded waits only (<= 2-3 s); kill every timer before returning. Consumer slice: Chrome, mstscax, quartz, dmusic, industrial apps; these are the top-value tests.

Multi-thread and lifetime semantics of timeSetEvent/timeKillEvent (and their interaction with timeBeginPeriod). 16-slot cap per process [decomp + VM]: create 16 periodic events (long delay 10000 ms) -> all nonzero and distinct, the 17th -> 0; kill one, then a new one succeeds; ids observed differ from killed ids. Run the cap test in a CHILD process so other tests' timers do not perturb it. TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS (0x100): callback sleeps 200 ms setting a flag on exit; kill from the main thread while the callback runs (signalled by an event from inside the callback) returns only after the flag is set; without 0x100 the kill may return early (t_note only). Kill from inside its own callback: timeKillEvent(own id) -> 0, no further callbacks (wait 200 ms, count unchanged), no deadlock (callback runs on the timer thread so SYNCHRONOUS must not wait on itself: verify in decomp). Callbacks are serialized on one worker thread: two periodic events record the same callback thread id and never overlap (interlocked in-callback counter max 1). timeSetEvent from several threads concurrently (4 x 4 events) returns distinct ids, then all kills -> 0. Each event holds a timeBeginPeriod(res) reference released at kill/fire: after setting and killing a 1 ms-resolution event, timeEndPeriod(1) with no own Begin -> 97 (the event's reference is gone; verify in decomp before CHECK). Callback calling timeGetTime/timeSetEvent (one-shot re-arm chain of 3) works. Process exit with a live periodic timer in a CHILD exits cleanly (exit code checked). Bounded waits, all timers killed.

Primary exports (must each get a real U()/UN() call): waveOutPrepareHeader, waveOutUnprepareHeader, waveOutWrite. WAVEHDR state machine (winmmbase waveOutPrepareHeader 0x10910, UnprepareHeader 0x109b0, Write 0x10a70), most of it headless because header checks precede the handle check [decomp + VM fc02probe]. Front gate for Prepare/Unprepare/Write: pwh NULL, cbwh < 0x30 (47), dwFlags & 0xFFFFCFE0 (e.g. 0x20, 0x100, 0x80000000) -> 11, before the handle. Prepare: already WHDR_PREPARED -> 0 without validating the handle (NULL handle -> 0); flags 0x1000|PREPARED -> 0; NULL handle unprepared -> 5. Unprepare: INQUEUE -> 33 (WAVERR_STILLPLAYING); not prepared -> 0 (any handle, no check); prepared + bad handle -> 5. Write: not prepared -> 34 (WAVERR_UNPREPARED); INQUEUE -> 33; prepared + bad handle -> 5. Prepare keeps only BEGINLOOP|ENDLOOP (dwFlags DONE|BEGINLOOP|ENDLOOP before -> BEGINLOOP|ENDLOOP|PREPARED after; device needed). cbwh larger than 48 (e.g. 64) accepted. Device half (Device gating: read the matching *GetNumDevs once at the start (first call may block while Audiosrv starts: never time it); always run the zero-device/contract half; run the device half only when n > 0 and t_note the count and caps names. ): prepare -> 0x2, write -> flags 0x12 right after (INQUEUE set synchronously), after completion 0x3 (DONE|PREPARED), INQUEUE cleared; dwBytesRecorded untouched for output (t_note); unprepare after done -> 0 and PREPARED cleared; write the same header twice while queued -> 33; unprepare while queued -> 33; zero-length buffer (dwBufferLength 0): t_note prepare/write results and that DONE arrives; buffer length not a multiple of nBlockAlign: t_note. Close with a queued buffer -> 33 and handle still valid; reset then close -> 0, all headers DONE and not INQUEUE. Silence only. Bounded waits on CALLBACK_EVENT (<= 3 s).
